audits.summary: The home page follows the 2.2553.1 greeting/stats-card structure, but every number on the card comes from a ledger kept by the Electron main process. That ledger only records forward from install, and only for threads created in this app. It is built from thread/tokenUsage/updated deltas, and with DeepSeek those deltas include prefix-cache hits, so token figures come out 4-6x too high on short sessions and more on long ones. The bridge stubs account/usage/read as {summary:null,daily:[]} (wrong field name, null summary) and account/rateLimits/read as all-null. As a result the card's account row always reads "Account usage unavailable", and the Usage page shows no daily table and no balance. This happens even though the Harness session logs (~/.dsh/sessions) store exact per-step usage with timestamps and provider/model, which is enough to rebuild the original full-history stats. The skeleton does not stay forever, but it is held for the whole Harness boot. The onboarding card, the What's new dialog and the account menu still carry Codex/ChatGPT assumptions.

The sidebar only lists ids in config.threadIds, loaded with one thread/read per id (main.jsx:793-812). The renderer never calls thread/list, even though it now returns every Harness session. As a result, sessions created in the official DeepSeek apps cannot be found, imported or resumed, because "/resume" only toggles the inline filter. The user's real profile also has 10 Codex-era ids that the DeepSeek core silently drops, while one archived Codex row is still listed but cannot be opened. On the bridge side: thread/list rows are incomplete (titles always null because of a result-shape bug, empty preview, updatedAt equal to createdAt, user forks classified as sub-agents); opening a session bumps its recency; auto-archive never fires; delete only hides the session although the UI says "permanently deleted"; and every session the user visits keeps a Harness write lock until Code Desktop exits.

The transcript renders DeepSeek output end to end: streamed text and reasoning, tool rows, code blocks and tables, turn footers and failed-turn cards all work. But the bridge only forwards part of what Harness produces. It ignores stream `block-end` chunks, tool abort info (`error.name: AbortError`), structured `LlmFailure` facts and retry counts, and the original Codex input part types (images, file mentions, skills). It also sends no token usage when a session is reopened. As a result the status row says "Thinking…" while the answer is visibly streaming (seen in the live screenshot). Pressing Stop turns running tools into "Failed to run" rows. Errors and retries all fall back to the generic labels. Attached images show up as raw bracket text. On the fidelity side, the reasoning row and the thinking status row still differ from the original in label, default open state, plain-text rendering, "Copy as quote", the "Thought for Ns" label and the click-to-show-thinking toggle.

The bridge (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/projection.js) covers the basics: bash becomes a terminal row, write/edit become diff cards, read/grep/glob become Read/Search rows, MCP tools map to mcpToolCall, and everything else falls back to dynamicToolCall. The existing tests only exercise the fallback path with no presenter, so several mappings that run whenever the real Harness presenters are present were never covered. Two of these are wrong in normal use. Every Read card shows the raw `N: ` line prefixes and the "(End of file …)" footer. Every web_search lands in the code-search branch and renders as "Searched" / "Searched code". On top of that, Harness tools with richer Codex/Claude equivalents still show up as raw "Used <tool>" rows: subagents, questions and plan review, todos, jobs and skills. Abort and denial outcomes are reported as "Failed". Bash descriptions and real edit line numbers are available but not used.

The basic approval loop works on DeepSeek. Ask mode's tools/pre-execute 'ask' goes through Harness approval/request to a Codex requestApproval. The tool call/item is projected before pre-execute, so file approvals find item.changes and show "Allow DeepSeek to write x?" (the live smoke covered this). Bypass maps to the danger-full-access preset, and requirements:null lets it through. The mode semantics are thin. Plan is only the read-only preset: Harness plan mode, exit_plan_mode and the user-questions review are never wired up, so escalation prompts can still allow edits during Plan. Session grants are keyed too broadly ('files' also covers sandbox escalations). Manual mode is not enforced for subagents. The card's reason, title and mode-menu text still differ from the source in ways that Harness data can now fix.

The composer, model menu and effort slider work against the bridge's model/list. It lists deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro, with off/low/high/max efforts that carry real descriptions, and no service tiers. Pressing Enter while a turn runs steers it correctly through agent.steer. The real breakage is in the bridge-backed actions the composer exposes. /compact always fails (the bridge calls dsh-commands execute() without its AbortSignal argument) and never emits a turn, which leaves the session locked. The Cmd+Enter queue lane and the queued-messages bar hit METHOD_NOT_FOUND, even though Harness has a durable inbox queue that maps one-to-one onto it. Image, mention and skill inputs are flattened into bracket text: the model has to re-read images with read_image, and the brackets then show up word for word in user bubbles and prompt history. /fork, /review and /rewind are offered but always rejected. On the fidelity side, the Fast mode section always shows as a disabled row (the original hides it when the model has no fast option), and there are a few invented catalog labels.

The Settings and Customize pages render, but on the DeepSeek core most of their data paths are empty or fail. The bridge (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js) returns [] for skills/list, mcpServerStatus/list and hooks/list, has no handler for config/read, plugin/*, skills/config/write or config/batchWrite, and reports {type:'apiKey'} without checking whether a key exists. Because of this the UI shows raw "X is not supported by the DeepSeek core yet." alerts, a Plugins error state that never clears, account and connector actions built for ChatGPT/Codex that always fail, and Codex paths (~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.codex/skills) that DeepSeek never reads. Harness already loads the services needed to fix this: ctx.skills (35 skills in ~/.agents/skills are already given to the model), ctx.credentials, ctx.deepseekAccount, ctx.configEditor/loader entries for dsh-mcp-client, and ctx.pluginManager. Most fixes are therefore bridge mappers plus core-aware copy and capability flags in the UI.

The bridge handles the core chat loop correctly: thread/start, resume and read, initialTurnsPage and turns/list paging, turn/start, steer and interrupt, streaming deltas, tool items, approvals and token usage, and ids stay consistent between live delivery and replay. The gaps are in the secondary protocol surface the app actually uses. thread/compact/start always throws, and because Harness compaction runs without a turn, it leaves the session stuck on 'Compacting conversation…' with the composer dead. Continuable sub-agents are invisible and cannot be stopped, and the 2 s background poll lists the whole session corpus because the sourceKinds filter does not match. thread/queue/*, thread/fork, skills/list and config/read return method-not-found or empty results even though Harness has matching primitives (inbox, buildForkSeed, ctx.skills, permission presets). Attachments are flattened to bracket text. Every sidebar thread/read replays the full log, and the 10 Codex-era ids in the user's profile fail with an opaque -32603 and silently drop out of the sidebar.

I checked the HANDOFF "剩余缺口/剩余差距" entries for 0.2.129 down to 0.2.93 against the current code in app/src. Most recent work went into test debt and pixel-level fidelity. The open everyday gaps are these: the collapsed-sidebar hover peek, session cycling (Ctrl+Tab, ⌘⇧[ and ⌘⇧], plus the Go menu items), the "More files" overflow menu in the Files tab strip, the Plan pane's task list styling, the Changes pane's file-list column and its word/whitespace toggles, and Ctrl+R history search in the composer. All of them can be built without Anthropic or Codex services. One backlog-adjacent area broke when the core moved to DeepSeek: the bridge does not implement the queue (thread/queue/*), so ⌘⏎ "send later" fails with an error. The Harness already has a durable Inbox and followup() that can back it. The Plan pane is now used much more often, because DeepSeek calls todo_write regularly, so its source-styling gap matters more than it did under Codex.

findings.title: Home token figures count DeepSeek prefix-cache hits (inflated 4-6x+ vs the original's input+output)
findings.userVisible: "Total tokens", the Models tab chart, per-model "{in} in · {out} out" and percentages, and the book footnote ("You've used ~N× more tokens than War and Peace") are several times too high after any multi-step DeepSeek turn.
findings.evidence: Original: reference/current-2.2553.1/asar/.vite/build/heavy-work-worker/heavyWorkWorker.js:1 (function ai) keeps input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read and cache_creation as separate buckets. Function ci then charts `let i=t.inputTokens+t.outputTokens` (cache excluded) as tokensByModel, and code-home.js:13711-13751 (Iw) sums only those. Harness TokenUsage is disjoint: dsh-llm/lib/types/types.d.ts:155-161 says 'inputTokens is uncached input only'. Bridge: harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:118-127 (addUsage) folds cacheRead+cacheWrite into inputTokens and adds the full usage.totalTokens. That is Codex-correct for the wire. Local ledger: app/electron/activity.cjs:36-47 charges the delta of total.totalTokens to day.models, and :50-54 records total.inputTokens (cache included) as modelUsage.input. home-model.mjs:115-139 sums these into totalTokens/modelTotals, and source-home.jsx:163 feeds bookSentence. Measured on the live-test sessions in ~/.dsh/sessions/--Users-oleyyu-claude-ui-lab-workspace--/: each step reports totalTokens of about 9k, of which cacheReadTokens is about 8.7k. A 5-step session is 45,618 total vs 9,906 input+output (4.6x); a 3-step session is 27,246 vs 4,334 (6.3x). The ratio grows with step count.
findings.fix: Charge the original's semantics in app/electron/activity.cjs: tokens delta = Δ(inputTokens − cachedInputTokens) + Δ(outputTokens), with the same per-field baseline rule already used for observedUsage. Store modelUsage.input as uncached input, with cached kept separately as it is now. Keep day.tokens consistent. Old ledger days were recorded with the inflated rule, so add a ledger version field (activity.version=2) and either exclude pre-v2 token entries or label them. If the logs-based stats from home-usage-full-history-stats land, the fold there must use usage.inputTokens + usage.outputTokens from Harness directly, and this ledger becomes the offline fallback.
findings.verification: Add a case to app/tests/activity.test.mjs: two thread/tokenUsage/updated events with total {totalTokens:8896,inputTokens:8836,cachedInputTokens:0,outputTokens:60} then {totalTokens:17871,inputTokens:17800,cachedInputTokens:8704,outputTokens:71}. Assert that day.models[model] === 8836+60+(260+11) and that modelUsage.input excludes the 8704 cached tokens. Run: cd app && node --test tests/activity.test.mjs tests/home-model.test.mjs

findings.title: account/usage/read returns {summary:null,daily:[]}: wrong shape, so the home account row is stuck on 'unavailable'
findings.userVisible: Under the stats card the account row always reads "Account usage unavailable. Showing activity recorded in this app.", and its "Refresh usage" button never helps. Every tile carries the "excludes earlier or other-client history" tooltip. Settings > Usage never shows the "Daily token usage" table.
findings.evidence: Bridge: harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:593-594 returns `{ summary: null, daily: [] }`. Protocol: analysis/codex-protocol/v2/GetAccountTokenUsageResponse.ts defines `{ summary: AccountTokenUsageSummary (non-null), dailyUsageBuckets: Array<{startDate:string,tokens}>|null, threadUsage? }`, and AccountTokenUsageSummary.ts defines `{lifetimeTokens, peakDailyTokens, longestRunningTurnSec, currentStreakDays, longestStreakDays}` (all nullable). UI: app/src/use-home-account-usage.jsx:12 throws when summary is not an object, which gives status 'error'. app/src/source-home.jsx:299-307 then renders the 'unavailable' row with an enabled Refresh button. home-account-usage.mjs:6-8 reads summary.lifetimeTokens and dailyUsageBuckets[{startDate,tokens}]. app/electron/usage-model.mjs:57 reads tokenUsage.dailyUsageBuckets for the Usage page table (source-usage.jsx:48). Harness has the data: every 'assistant/message' event carries `time` (dsh-session/lib/types/types.d.ts:489-496), `data.usage` and `data.message.source.{provider,model}` (types.d.ts:330-338). Sessions are enumerable via sessionQuery.listSessions()/readSession() (dsh-session-query/lib/types/index.d.ts:67-74), and ctx.sessionPersistence.list() gives an opaque per-session `revision` for caching (dsh-session-persistence/lib/types/index.d.ts:22-31). Retried attempts can be folded with deriveTurnTokenUsage from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter/client' (lib/types/turn-usage.d.ts).
findings.fix: Add harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/usage.js containing two pure functions. foldSessionUsage(header, events) folds one session into a summary keyed by local day: tokens = usage.inputTokens + usage.outputTokens per assistant/message, plus the usage of the last chunk of each assistant/attempt; per-model input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite; turn durations from turn/start→turn/end. accountTokenUsage(summaries, today) returns {summary:{lifetimeTokens, peakDailyTokens, longestRunningTurnSec, currentStreakDays, longestStreakDays}, dailyUsageBuckets:[{startDate,tokens}] sorted, threadUsage:null}. In index.js, answer account/usage/read from these folds over listSessions(), skipping store.get(id).deleted. Cache per (sessionId, persistence revision) in memory and optionally in ~/.dsh/code-desktop/usage-cache.json. For live threads, fold the in-memory events. Keep the response integer-safe, because home-account-usage.mjs rejects non-safe integers.
findings.verification: New harness/tests/usage.test.mjs: feed synthetic events (turn/start, user/message, assistant/message with usage {inputTokens:260,outputTokens:11,cacheReadTokens:8704,totalTokens:8975} and time on two local days, plus turn/end). Assert the exact response shape and that bucket tokens exclude cache reads. Then cd app && node --test tests/home-account-usage.test.mjs with a fixture equal to that output, asserting accountActivity(...).totalTokens and activeDays. Run: cd harness && node --test tests/usage.test.mjs

findings.title: Stats card is a forward-only, this-app-only ledger; the original is full 182-day transcript history and Harness logs allow an exact port
findings.userVisible: On a fresh install, or for sessions started in the official DeepSeek Harness app, the card shows 0 sessions/messages/tokens, "—" peak hour and favorite model, and an empty heatmap, even though months of DeepSeek history exist on disk. Peak hour is computed per message instead of per session start. Sub-agent token spend is never counted. The card also carries an adaptation row and native title tooltips that the original does not have.
findings.evidence: Original: heavyWorkWorker.js:1 (function ci) scans every transcript modified in the last 182 days (157248e5 ms). It counts a session per file by first timestamp, and hourCounts by session-start hour (`let i=n.getHours();d.set(i,(d.get(i)??0)+1)`). Messages are all user/assistant entries. Files under subagents/ contribute tokens but not sessions. It returns {totalSessions,totalMessages,activeDays,firstSessionDate,lastSessionDate,peakActivityHour,streaks,dailyActivity,dailyModelTokens,modelUsage}. code-home.js:13711-13751 (Iw) aggregates it; Yw/Xw at :13925-14031 renders only the tabs, six tiles, the eT heatmap and the footnote, with no account/source row and no tile titles ($w :14071). Local: app/electron/activity.cjs:1-3, 11 says 'Forward-only', records only config.threadIds, and gets token usage only from live notifications. home-model.mjs:113-114 builds peak hour from per-message hour counts. source-home.jsx:117-123 uses native `title={description}` on tiles, :164 adds the localScope copy, and :299-307 adds the 'Tokens and active days: account… / Account usage unavailable' row with Refresh. HANDOFF.md:1027 lists '完整历史统计' (full-history stats) as still open. Harness equivalent: session logs carry exact time, usage and source.model per step; header.origin==='subagent' marks sub-agent sessions (used in index.js:752).
findings.fix: Reuse the per-session fold from home-usage-account-usage-read-stub, extended with sessionCount (first human user/message time, non-subagent), messageCount (user/message + assistant/message), toolCallCount (tool/call) and hourCounts by session start. Add a bridge method (e.g. `codeDesktop/usageStats/read`, allow-listed in app/electron/main.cjs) returning exactly the original payload shape over the last 182 days. Map model ids to wire ids via catalog.wireId(provider, model) so modelDisplayName resolves. In main.cjs 'stats', return {source:'harness', stats} when connected, falling back to the ledger. In home-model.mjs, add an Iw port (aggregateStats) over dailyActivity/dailyModelTokens/modelUsage. In source-home.jsx, render the original Xw (peakActivityHour from stats, heatmap from dailyActivity.messageCount). Remove the account source row and the tile title attributes when the Harness source is used.
findings.verification: harness/tests/usage-stats.test.mjs: two parent sessions plus one subagent session across two days. Assert totalSessions=2 (subagent excluded), subagent tokens are included in dailyModelTokens, peakActivityHour equals the session-start hour (not the busiest message hour), and streaks are correct. app/tests/home-model.test.mjs: aggregateStats(payload,'7d',today) matches Iw (sessions/messages/activeDays in range, 0.05% model cutoff, modelUsage all-time). Run: cd harness && node --test tests/usage-stats.test.mjs ; cd app && node --test tests/home-model.test.mjs. Then run the offscreen app/scripts/home-page-ui-test.mjs to check that the six tiles have no [title].

findings.title: Stats skeleton is held for the whole Harness boot because the local ledger read waits for the core connection
findings.userVisible: On every launch the home card shows the qw skeleton next to "Connecting to DeepSeek…" for the 2-4 s Harness boot. If the core hangs it can last up to the 30 s initialize timeout, or the 120 s model/list request timeout. This is despite the stats being local data.
findings.evidence: Local: app/src/main.jsx:745-749 does `const b = await call("init"); setBoot(b); loadStats();`, so loadStats starts only after init resolves. app/electron/main.cjs:426-429 has the 'init' handler await `connect()`, which waits for initialize (codex.cjs:118-125, 30000 ms) and then account/read + model/list (main.cjs:210-212, request default 120000 ms in codex.cjs:175). Yet the 'stats' IPC (main.cjs:632-636) only reads config.activity. harness/README.md:73 documents the 2-4 s boot. work/deepseek-live-20261001/first-mupaykl9/01-home.png shows the skeleton card together with "Connecting to DeepSeek…". Original: the stats come from the heavy-work worker scan, independent of any agent connection, and Rw (code-home.js:13755-13761) only shows qw while that query is pending.
findings.fix: In app/src/main.jsx, start loadStats() in the mount effect in parallel with init(), next to the existing `call("home-shape")` at ~line 831, and stop chaining it after `await call("init")`. The 'stats' push event (main.cjs:195) still refreshes it after turns. If the Harness stats source from home-usage-full-history-stats is added, show the ledger snapshot immediately and swap in the Harness payload once connected.
findings.verification: New app/tests/home-stats-load.test.mjs (same style as composer-placeholder.test.mjs, which reads src/main.jsx): assert that loadStats() is invoked in the mount effect and not only after `await call("init")`. Run: cd app && node --test tests/home-stats-load.test.mjs. Optionally extend app/scripts/home-page-ui-test.mjs with a slow fake core (CODEX_BINARY) and assert that [data-testid=epitaxy-stats-card] renders while .connection-card still says Connecting.

findings.title: account/read always reports an API key; the no-key path is undetected and the setup card is a dead ChatGPT sign-in
findings.userVisible: A user without a DeepSeek key sees a normal ready home, and the first message then fails with a credential error. If requiresOpenaiAuth ever is true, the home card says "Set up DeepSeek — Continue with your ChatGPT account", and its Sign in button always errors with "DeepSeek uses an API key…".
findings.evidence: Bridge: harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:583-588 returns {account:{type:'apiKey'}} whenever ctx.llm.listProviders() is non-empty. Per harness/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek-api-key/README.md:28, 'Model discovery returns the configured catalog regardless of credentials' and requests fail with MISSING_CREDENTIAL, so that check is always true. index.js:595-598 throws METHOD_NOT_FOUND for account/login/start. UI: app/src/main.jsx:2142-2160 renders the ChatGPT card, and Sign in calls call('login'), which goes to main.cjs:841 and then app/electron/account-operations.cjs:28, which only accepts chatgpt types. Available in Harness: ctx.credentials.describe(ref) → {configured} (dsh-credentials/lib/types/index.d.ts:136) and ctx.deepseekAccount.getState() → status 'signed-out'|'credential-stored' (dsh-deepseek-account/lib/types/index.d.ts, types.d.ts:28-32). The Codex protocol already has LoginAccountParams {type:'apiKey', apiKey} → LoginAccountResponse {type:'apiKey'} (analysis/codex-protocol/v2/LoginAccountParams.ts, LoginAccountResponse.ts).
findings.fix: Bridge: add a pure helper accountReadResult({keyConfigured, accountStatus, providers}). account/read awaits ctx.credentials.describe('DEEPSEEK_API_KEY') and ctx.get('deepseekAccount')?.getState(), and returns {account:null, requiresOpenaiAuth:true} when neither is configured. Implement account/login/start {type:'apiKey', apiKey} via ctx.credentials.set, then notify account/updated and account/login/completed {success:true}. App: account-operations.cjs accepts 'apiKey' (no browser step). Replace the main.jsx card copy with "Add your DeepSeek API key", a password field and Save (call('login',{type:'apiKey',apiKey})), plus a hint that keys saved in DeepSeek Harness (~/.dsh) are picked up automatically.
findings.verification: harness/tests/account.test.mjs: accountReadResult({keyConfigured:false, accountStatus:'signed-out'}) → {account:null, requiresOpenaiAuth:true}; with keyConfigured:true → apiKey. app/tests/account-operations.test.mjs: start('apiKey') sends account/login/start {type:'apiKey'} and does not call openExternal. Add a wiring assertion that main.jsx no longer contains 'Continue with your ChatGPT account'. Run: cd harness && node --test tests/account.test.mjs ; cd app && node --test tests/account-operations.test.mjs

findings.title: Rate-limit read is an empty snapshot; the DeepSeek wallet balance Harness exposes is never shown
findings.userVisible: Settings > Usage shows only "Usage limits are unavailable for this account or connection." with no balance. The tray and account surfaces have no DeepSeek credit information.
findings.evidence: Bridge: harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:589-592 returns an all-null RateLimitSnapshot. UI already renders credits: app/electron/usage-model.mjs:44-50 maps rateLimits.credits {hasCredits, unlimited, balance} to a 'Usage credits' section (app/src/source-usage.jsx:40-43). Protocol: analysis/codex-protocol/v2/CreditsSnapshot.ts {hasCredits:boolean, unlimited:boolean, balance:string|null}. Harness: ctx.deepseekAccount.getBalance(client) → {status:'ready', value: AccountWallet[], bonusWallets: AccountWallet[]} with {currency:'CNY'|'USD', balance:string} (dsh-deepseek-account/lib/types/index.d.ts:50; types.d.ts:43-63), mounted by dsh-base (dsh-base/cordis.patch.yml:112-113). Caveat: this works only after DeepSeek Platform sign-in. There is no API-key balance call in Harness (no 'user/balance' anywhere in vendor/deepseek-harness).
findings.fix: In the bridge, when ctx.get('deepseekAccount') state is 'credential-stored', call getBalance({version, locale:'en-US', timezoneOffsetSeconds}). Return rateLimits = {limitId:'deepseek', limitName:'DeepSeek', primary:null, secondary:null, credits:{hasCredits: any wallet > 0, unlimited:false, balance:'¥12.34' (+ bonus)}, …null}, and keep the empty snapshot otherwise. Optionally, behind an explicit setting, fetch DeepSeek's GET /user/balance with the resolved API key for key-only users. In source-usage.jsx, replace the 'unavailable' line with 'DeepSeek API is pay-as-you-go; there are no usage windows.' when the limitId is 'deepseek'.
findings.verification: harness/tests/account.test.mjs: rateLimitsFromBalance({status:'ready', value:[{currency:'CNY',balance:'12.34'}], bonusWallets:[{currency:'CNY',balance:'5.00'}]}) → credits.balance contains '12.34' and hasCredits true; {status:'failed'} → credits null. app/tests/usage-model.test.mjs: usagePresentation({limits:{rateLimits:{limitId:'deepseek',credits:{hasCredits:true,unlimited:false,balance:'¥12.34'}}}}) yields one credits row. Run: cd harness && node --test tests/account.test.mjs ; cd app && node --test tests/usage-model.test.mjs

findings.title: Account menu header reads 'DeepSeek · DeepSeek'; label logic still keyed on ChatGPT plan
findings.userVisible: Opening the account menu from the "Local · DeepSeek" footer shows a second header line "DeepSeek · DeepSeek".
findings.evidence: Local: app/src/main.jsx:1661-1664 sets accountLabel = chatgpt ? planType || 'DeepSeek API' : 'DeepSeek', so an apiKey account gives 'DeepSeek'. main.jsx:1923 renders `{accountLabel} · DeepSeek`, and source-sidebar.jsx:1061-1065 renders the footer as `{accountName} · {accountLabel}`. Original: sidebar-rows.js:16560-16575 (tV) renders the identity line and then an org line `orgPrimary · orgSecondary` (or just orgPrimary) with data-testid='user-menu-header-org'. The footer pw (sidebar-groups.js:5225-5240) shows identity · orgPrimary. Bridge account/read already returns a non-Codex `provider` name string (index.js:586), and Harness deepseekAccount.getProfile() gives {name, contact} when signed in (dsh-deepseek-account/lib/types/index.d.ts:44, types.d.ts:36-42).

findings.title: Opening a session resets its 'last activity'; inactivity auto-archive never fires with the DeepSeek core
findings.userVisible: Opening an old session without sending anything makes the core report it as updated now: archived rows from threadMetadata move to Today, and after a restart a permission-preset change can move it too. Settings → "Archive inactive sessions after N days" silently does nothing.
findings.evidence: BRIDGE: harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:82 sets LiveThread.lastActivityMs = Date.now() at construction and hydrate (86-92) never resets it; index.js:99 bumps it on every live event; threadObject uses it at 488. index.js:428 applyPermissions on thread/resume can append 'permission/preset' (dsh-permission-presets/lib/types/index.d.ts:180-186), and projection.js:327-328 advances updatedAtMs on every event type, including session/title (415-420), so the persisted log also moves. index.js:489 reports every session not opened in this process as {type:'notLoaded'}. LOCAL: main.cjs:522-524 writes the resume response (updatedAt=now) into config.threadMetadata, which feeds archived rows (main.jsx:804-807). desktop-settings.cjs:21 sweep skips unless status.type==='idle' and the age exceeds N days, so unloaded sessions are always skipped and loaded ones look fresh. UPSTREAM: list.ts:327-329 updatedAt = max(createdAt, lastPromptAt), where lastPromptAt moves only on human user/message (45-56). ORIGINAL picker sorts on lastActivityAt (cc43287c9:24928).
findings.fix: projection.js: add lastActivityMs that advances only on user/message with source.kind==='user', turn/start, assistant/message and turn/end; leave updatedAtMs for internal use. index.js: start LiveThread.lastActivityMs as null and set it from projector.lastActivityMs after hydrate; in onEvent bump only for those event types; threadObject uses live?.lastActivityMs ?? projector?.lastActivityMs ?? cached lastPromptAt ?? createdMs. desktop-settings.cjs:21: also treat 'notLoaded' as quiescent (`!['idle','notLoaded'].includes(thread.status?.type)`). A thread this core has not loaded has no agent or terminals here, and the existing background/child/worktree checks still apply.

findings.title: Every visited session keeps its Harness write lock until Code Desktop quits; a session busy in another DeepSeek app fails with a raw error
findings.userVisible: After the user merely views a session in Code Desktop, the official DeepSeek app cannot continue that session until Code Desktop exits (SessionAlreadyOwnedError). Opening a session that is still open in the official app shows a raw core error in the transcript instead of the source's "Can't confirm it's closed" status.
findings.evidence: BRIDGE: index.js:379-415 openThread resumes with ctx.agents.resume (390), and the LiveThread stays in `threads` until thread/delete (662-671) or thread/close/unsubscribe (673-682). The jsonl backend holds a kernel flock on session.lock for the life of the write handle; contention maps to SessionAlreadyOwnedError (dsh-session-persistence-jsonl/lib/types/lease.d.ts:1-13; errors.d.ts:21-26). The error reaches the client unmapped. LOCAL: no thread/unsubscribe or thread/close anywhere in app/src or app/electron; the main.cjs:89-121 allowlist omits them. main.jsx:1088-1096 shows the raw message as loadError. ORIGINAL: the picker marks sessions whose liveness is unknown as "Can't confirm it's closed" and skips running ones (cc43287c9:24608, 25124-25135, be(e)).
findings.fix: App: add "thread/unsubscribe" to the main.cjs allowlist. In main.jsx openSession/navigate, when leaving a session that is idle (no state.active, no pending approval or queue), send thread/unsubscribe for it and remove it from resumed.current. turn/start already re-opens through openThread (index.js:684), so later sends still work. Put the policy in a pure app/src/session-unload-model.mjs. Bridge: in openThread, catch SessionAlreadyOwnedError (by error.name) and throw RpcError(-32000, 'This session is open in another DeepSeek app. Close it there, then try again.', {codexErrorInfo:'sessionBusyElsewhere'}). Optionally add an idle reaper that closes LiveThreads idle for more than 10 minutes with no pendingApprovals and agent.status !== 'running'.

findings.userVisible: The sidebar skeleton stays up for longer as history grows: each owned session costs a full read and replay of its log. Official-app sessions reach tens of thousands of events (one is at seq 84491), so adopting them through the resume picker would make startup visibly slow.

BRIDGE: index.js:618-621 thread/read → historyFor (452-470) → sessionQuery.readSession, which reads and replay-validates the complete raw log (dsh-session-query/lib/types/index.d.ts readSession doc), then a new ThreadProjector applies every event (468-469) even though turns are discarded. ~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/sessions/session-9c922c3d…json reports title seq 84491. findings.title: Reasoning/text items stay 'streaming' until the whole step commits, so the status row says "Thinking…" while the answer streams
findings.userVisible: Every DeepSeek turn that uses reasoning (effort above off) shows "Thinking…" in the status row, escalating to "Still thinking…" and then "Almost done thinking…" as the turn goes on, while the final answer is visibly streaming. The same happens while tool-call arguments stream. The live run captured it: work/deepseek-live-20261001/first-mupaykl9/03a-streaming.png shows "2s · Thinking…" under a half-written answer. If an attempt fails and is not retried, the failed attempt's reasoning text also stays visible.
findings.evidence: Harness: the DeepSeek adapter yields a `block-end` chunk carrying the assembled block for every reasoning, text and tool block (harness/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1961-1975; StreamChunk type at dsh-llm/lib/types/types.d.ts:417-447). The step's assistant/message is only appended after the whole stream finishes (dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:1069-1079 and 1122ff). Bridge: LiveThread.onStream handles only `block-start`, `text-delta` and `reasoning-delta`, so `block-end` is dropped (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:194-206). Items are closed only by the projector's `assistant/message` case (projection.js:347-364). The abandoned-attempt body for reasoning omits `reasoningText` (index.js:186-188), so the reducer merge keeps stale deltas (app/src/state.js:456). App: phases stay 'streaming' until item/completed (state.js:466-468, 495-497). turnActivityLabel returns the thinking ladder whenever any reasoning item of the turn is still streaming (app/src/transcript-runtime-stats.mjs:60-67), and the status row shows it (app/src/source-transcript-status.jsx:31,95). Original: thinking is 'active' only while a thinking block is open (approval-shared-current.js:1969-1981, Du with thinkingStart).
findings.fix: 1) Move the live frame-to-notification mapping out of LiveThread.onStream into a pure, exported class in harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/projection.js (input: frame plus a turnIdFor callback; output: notes) so it can be unit-tested. index.js then only calls it and notifies. 2) On `chunk.type === 'block-end'` for a reasoning or text block, emit `item/completed` with `{type:'reasoning', id, summary:[block.text], content:[]}` or `{type:'agentMessage', id, text: block.text, …}` and `completedAtMs: frame.time`. 3) In the abandoned-attempt branch, add `reasoningText: ''` to the cleared reasoning body. 4) Optional defensive change in app/src/transcript-runtime-stats.mjs: return the thinking label only when the newest streaming item of the turn is reasoning, not when a later agentMessage in the same turn is streaming.
findings.verification: cd harness && node --test tests/projection.test.mjs: a new test feeds frames start, then block-start/reasoning-delta/block-end for reasoning index 0, then block-start/text-delta for text index 1. It asserts item/completed for msg-1.1.0 (summary = full text) arrives before item/started for msg-1.1.1, and that a non-committed end clears reasoningText. cd app && node --test tests/transcript-runtime-stats.test.mjs: reduce the same notification sequence through state.js reduce and assert turnActivityLabel(turnId, items, phases, 20) === null while the agentMessage streams, and still 'Still thinking…' while only reasoning streams.

findings.title: Stop turns running and queued tools into "Failed to run … / Error: tool call aborted" rows instead of "Stopped"
findings.userVisible: When the user presses Stop during tool execution, the running command or edit row turns into "Failed to run …" with "Error: tool call aborted" as its output. Calls the model had requested but not yet started show up as new failed rows after the Stop. Group summaries count them as "(N failed)". After reopening the session, any leftover in-progress tool reads as failed. The original shows these rows as "Stopped" (muted).
findings.evidence: Harness: an aborted tool resolves to `{content:'Error: tool call aborted', isError:true, error:{info:{name:'AbortError', code:'ABORTED'}}}` (dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3675-3692), or to ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH (3694-3711). On abort, every unstarted call gets a durable tool/call plus tool/result pair (dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:645-651, 662-679), and `data.error` carries the info (690-706). Bridge: the tool/result case ignores `data.error` (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/projection.js:381-395), and completeToolItem maps any isError to 'failed' (projection.js:188, 198-221, 239-242). turn/end turns leftover inProgress items into 'failed' even for aborted turns (projection.js:445-449), and harness/tests/projection.test.mjs:59-61 asserts that. App: the live reducer settles an interrupted turn's running items as 'interrupted' (app/src/state.js:411-414), and 'interrupted' renders as "Stopped" (app/src/command-row-model.mjs:32,43; source-session.jsx:208-211; file-tool-model.mjs:129-131 excludes interruptions from failure counts). Original: the tool row shows "Stopped" (reference/current-2.2553.1/readable/approval-current.js:17213-17222).
findings.fix: In harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/projection.js, pass `data.error` from the tool/result case into completeToolItem. When `error?.name === 'AbortError'` (codes ABORTED and ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH), return `status:'interrupted'` for every item type, with no error body: aggregatedOutput null and exitCode null for commands, no `error` for fileChange, contentItems [] and success null for dynamic tools. In the turn/end case, settle leftover inProgress items to 'interrupted' when turnStatusOf(reason) === 'interrupted' and to 'failed' otherwise, and update the projection.test.mjs expectation. No app change is needed because 'interrupted' already maps to the "Stopped" state.
findings.verification: cd harness && node --test tests/projection.test.mjs: (a) tool/call bash plus tool/result {isError:true, content 'Error: tool call aborted'} with data.error {name:'AbortError', code:'ABORTED'} gives item.status 'interrupted' and aggregatedOutput null; (b) the same with code ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH; (c) an aborted turn/end with a running todo_write gives 'interrupted'. cd app && node --test tests/command-row-model.test.mjs tests/tool-group-presentation.test.mjs: commandRowState({status:'interrupted'}) === 'stopped', and a group with one interrupted read has no '(1 failed)'.

findings.title: DeepSeek failure codes, HTTP status and retry counts are dropped: every retry reads "Request failed · Retrying…" and every failure gets the generic card
findings.userVisible: An exhausted DeepSeek balance (HTTP 402), an invalid API key (401), a context overflow, a rate limit or a 5xx all produce the same card: "An API error occurred", "Try sending your message again." and a Retry button. For billing and auth errors that advice cannot work. Retries always read "Request failed · Retrying…", where the original reads "{short error} · Retrying (n/max)".
findings.evidence: Harness: providerError classifies AUTH, QUOTA (402 or insufficient balance), RATE_LIMIT, CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED, INVALID_REQUEST and SERVER, plus `status` and `requestId` (dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1743-1765). The retryable set and other codes are at dsh-llm/lib/index.js:136-160 and 249-256. llm/retry carries retry, maxRetries, delayMs and failure (dsh-llm-retry/lib/types/types.d.ts, LlmRetryEventData). Bridge: turnError always sends `codexErrorInfo:null` and puts the code in additionalDetails (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/projection.js:52-61). llm/retry sends only a message with codexErrorInfo null and drops the counts (projection.js:421-431). agent/error does the same (index.js:267-272). 'max-tokens' is silently mapped to 'completed' (projection.js:63-68). App: classifyTurnError(null) returns 'unknown' (app/src/turn-error-model.mjs:20-41). TABLE has no billing or output-limit category, and its auth hint is "Sign in again to continue." findings.title: /compact always fails and leaves the session locked: bridge omits the AbortSignal and never emits a compact turn

findings.evidence: Bridge: harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:708-716 calls commands.execute(thread.agent, '/compact', []) with 3 arguments, returns {} at once and ignores the CommandResult. Harness API: harness/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands/lib/types/index.d.ts:142 is execute(agent, line, submittedAttachments, signal: AbortSignal). The implementation, dsh-commands/lib/index.js:327-332, reads `signal.aborted`, which throws a TypeError when signal is undefined. Results are {kind:'success'|'error', text} (dsh-commands/lib/types/types.d.ts:33-41). dsh-command-compact/README.md:12 says compaction 'does not consume a model turn'. harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/projection.js:400-402 drops compaction/start when no turn is in progress, so no turn/started or turn/completed is ever sent. App: app/electron/session-operations.cjs:173-183 leaves 'starting' only when it gets result.turn.id or turn/started (observe :77-99). The pending entry makes assertAvailable/reserveMessage throw (:61-69), and turn/start uses that check (app/electron/main.cjs:511). app/src/session-command-model.mjs:81 operationPending('starting') feeds sending={sending||actionPending} (app/src/main.jsx:2276). plan.overview:
Plan for the DeepSeek-core gaps and the remaining Claude Desktop fidelity work.

Spot-checks confirmed every high-severity claim I tested:
- harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js:712 calls `commands.execute()` with 3 arguments. dsh-commands/lib/index.js:332 reads `signal.aborted` without a guard, so `/compact` always throws. It returns `{}` with no turn, so session-operations.cjs:119-183 keeps the lock forever.
- index.js:194-206 drops `block-end` chunks, although the DeepSeek adapter emits them (dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1971).
- projection.js ignores tool/result `data.error`. The AbortError info is persisted at dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:696-706, and `approval/asked` / `approval/decided` events are durable.
- projection.js:208-210 renders the read body with its `N:` prefixes and footer. Confirmed against dsh-tool-fs formatReadOutput and presentResult.
- `web_search` matches the grep/glob branch first (projection.js:143 versus dsh-tool-web presentSearchCall `kind: 'search'`).
- account/read, account/usage/read, skills/list and the queue stubs behave as the audits describe.

New issue found while checking: Electron `ipcRenderer.invoke` drops `error.data`. As a result `isNotSteerable` (queued-messages-model.mjs:102) can never see `activeTurnNotSteerable`, and the renderer cannot see `threadNotFound`. Batch 2 adds an RPC error passthrough that batches 3 and 9 rely on.

Duplicates merged:
- compact: 2 findings
- queue: 3 findings
- abort/reject status: 2 findings
- subagents: 3 findings, including the Ask-mode bypass for child agents
- user-input round trip and images: 4 findings
- skills: settings page plus bridge
- config/read: 2 findings
- account: API-key page plus no-key onboarding
- usage: account/usage/read stub plus Usage tab
- additional folders: 2 findings
- Codex sessions vanishing plus the thread/read not-found case

Ordering:
- Batches 1-8 fix high-severity behaviour broken on the DeepSeek core: stream and tool outcomes, compact/queue, core capabilities and legacy sessions, Plan mode and questions, approvals, sub-agents, settings catalog, account/usage.
- Batches 9-11 are medium DeepSeek degradations plus closely related fidelity work.
- Batch 12 is fidelity polish. The What's new notes go there on purpose, so the release notes describe the final state after all earlier batches.

Shared conventions every batch must keep:
- Testable bridge logic lives in pure modules under harness/packages/codex-app-server/src. index.js binds stdin/stdout at apply, so it cannot be unit-tested directly.
- `cd harness && node --test tests/projection.test.mjs` must stay green after every batch.
- Batch 3 introduces `boot.core` = {engine, engineVersion, capabilities, configPath}. Later batches extend `CAPABILITIES` in index.js and read `boot.core` in the app. They do not invent new plumbing.
- Batch 3 creates src/errors.js. Later batches add to it instead of creating new error helpers.

Deferred items are either L-effort fidelity work or depend on data Harness does not provide.

batches.name: B1 bridge stream and tool outcomes
batches.goal: Close reasoning and text items when their stream block ends. Show Stop and Deny as Stopped/Denied rather than Failed. Clean up Read cards, route web_search correctly, and replay token usage and plan when a session is reopened.
batches.instructions:
1) LIVE STREAM MAPPER.
- Move the logic of LiveThread.onStream/emitStart (index.js:170-224) and its `streams` map into a new exported class `LiveStreamMapper` in projection.js.
- Interface: `constructor({threadId, projector})`, `frame(frame, nowMs)` returning an array of {method, params}, and `endTurn(dshTurn)`, which replaces index.js:113-115.
- Keep current behaviour unchanged:
  - a retried attempt re-emits item/started (reset) for the previous attempt's items;
  - ensureTurn runs when the Codex turn has no id yet;
  - non-committed `end` clears its items.
- NEW, chunk.type==='block-end' for a known stream item with chunk.block?.type 'reasoning' or 'text': emit item/completed with completedAtMs = nowMs.
  - reasoning item: {type:'reasoning', id, summary:[chunk.block.text ?? ''], content:[]}
  - text item: {type:'agentMessage', id, text: chunk.block.text ?? '', phase:null, memoryCitation:null, delivery:null, questions:null}
  - id: assistantItemId(turn, step, index)
  - Ignore tool-call blocks.
- NEW, in the abandoned-attempt branch, the cleared reasoning body also carries reasoningText:''.
- index.js: LiveThread owns `this.stream = new LiveStreamMapper(...)`. onStream returns early while hydrating, otherwise notifies every note. The later committed assistant/message still emits item/completed; the reducer merges by id, so the duplicate is harmless.

2) TOOL OUTCOMES.
- In ThreadProjector.apply, track `approval/asked` (data.id → data.callId). On `approval/decided` with outcome 'rejected', add that callId to `this.rejectedCalls`.
- In the tool/result case, pass `error: data.error` and `rejected: this.rejectedCalls.has(message.toolCallId)` into completeToolItem.
- In completeToolItem, set `aborted = error?.name === 'AbortError'` (codes ABORTED and ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH). Fallback for logs without error info: content text exactly 'Error: tool call aborted' or 'Error: tool call aborted before dispatch'.
- When aborted, return status 'interrupted' with no error body:
  - commandExecution: aggregatedOutput null, exitCode null, keep durationMs;
  - fileChange: no `error` field;
  - webSearch: status only;
  - mcpToolCall: result null, error null;
  - dynamic: contentItems [], success null.
- When rejected and not aborted:
  - commandExecution and fileChange get status 'declined' (commands: aggregatedOutput null, exitCode null; fileChange: no error);
  - other types stay 'failed' with success:false.
- In the turn/end case (projection.js:447-449), settle leftover inProgress items to 'interrupted' when turn.status==='interrupted', else 'failed'.
- Update the assertion at harness/tests/projection.test.mjs:60 to expect 'interrupted'.

3) READ CARD. In completeToolItem's `view?.card === 'read'` branch:
- When Array.isArray(view.lines), set aggregatedOutput = view.lines.map(l => `${l.number}: ${l.text}`).join('\n').
- Otherwise strip the footer from textOf(view.content).
- Extend the footer regex at projection.js:205 so it also matches '(Output capped. …)' (dsh-tool-fs formatReadOutput emits that variant). Use the same regex in both branches.

4) WEB AND GLOB.
- In toolItem, move the `name === 'web_search' || name === 'web_fetch' || kind === 'fetch'` branch ABOVE the search branch.
- Restrict the search branch to `name === 'grep' || name === 'glob' || (kind === 'search' && !Array.isArray(args?.queries))`.
- Map glob to the action {type:'search', command, query: args?.pattern ?? null, path}, so the row reads 'Searched <pattern>' as in the source Glob label.
- webSearch items start with status:'inProgress'.
- In completeToolItem webSearch, status = aborted ? 'interrupted' : failed ? 'failed' : 'completed'.
